key_insight: An integrated translational bioinformatics and machine learning pipeline can combine RNA-seq and whole-genome sequencing to find biomarkers, predict disease risk, and profile patients for precision medicine.
clinical_relevance: The framework may help identify higher-risk patients earlier and support more personalized diagnosis and prevention strategies across diverse populations.
method: Analyzed blood-derived multi-omics data, including RNA-seq and whole-genome sequencing.
Used bioinformatics pipelines to detect differentially expressed genes and pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants.
Applied machine learning for biomarker discovery, disease prediction, clustering, patient profiling, and pathogenicity classification.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that results were validated against clinical records and state-of-the-science literature, with gene-disease associations and shared pathways identified across the broader population.
watch_item: The abstract does not provide external prospective validation or deployment details, so real-world generalizability and clinical implementation remain uncertain.
paper_title: Translational bioinformatics and machine learning framework for biomarker discovery, disease prediction, and patient profiling for precision medicine
